axis_supply.supply_status: ADEQUATE for defensive operations, STRAINED for sustained offensive. Ramcke Brigade elite formation but light brigade structure = limited logistics. Arrived North Africa July 1942 with full equipment, but no resupply echelon established. Dependent on German DAK logistics network and Italian X Corps (assigned Italian corps Q3). Brigade mobility CRITICAL - must move rapidly to threatened sectors. Fuel reserves 5 days (light vehicles only - no tanks). Ammunition 7 days (heavy expenditure expected - elite assault troops). Water 12L/man/day (adequate for summer heat vs Italian 8-10L/day). Supply base: Benghazi (600km), Tripoli (1,000km). RAF/Malta convoy attacks affecting resupply. CRITICAL ISSUE: Brigade uses captured British trucks (156 of 358 total) - spare parts unavailable, mechanical failures increasing Q3. German trucks insufficient for brigade needs. Water shortage chronic - desert summer 38°C max temperature. Medical supplies adequate (paratroop priority). Ammunition adequate for defensive but insufficient for prolonged offensive. Morale HIGH (elite troops) but supply constraints limiting operational effectiveness.

notes: Integrated into British 8th Army supply system
El Alamein defensive posture - static defense, low fuel consumption
